title: Model catalog: curated per-model quant defaults with confidence metrics and rollback guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and ship a curated set of per-model quantization defaults (FP8/INT8) in the model catalog that include a confidence metric and automated rollback guardrails. Deliver a reproducible calibration workflow, validation harness, and telemetry contract so Console and API teams can surface recommended profiles and enforce safe fallbacks.

Scope: covers hosted and Dedicated catalog entries (catalog metadata schema, runtime flags, calibration artifact storage). Private on-prem packaging is out-of-scope for this ticket but the catalog schema must be compatible with Private ingestion. This work will not change runtime kernels; it defines defaults, telemetry, and guardrail policies that the serving runtime will consume in a follow-up integration ticket.
background: We currently allow manual per-deployment quant selection which leads to operational regressions (quality drops, silent regressions). Existing quant presets are inconsistent across model families and lack a confidence signal. Prior tickets (ENG-9274, ENG-10512) introduced quant tuning and per-model defaults prototypes; this ticket consolidates those learnings into a production curation playbook, with standardized metrics, a calibration CI job, and automatic rollback thresholds for catalog-sourced profiles.
decisions: Adopt two-tier default model profiles: 'recommended' (aggressive cost/speed target, requires higher confidence score) and 'safe' (conservative, lower risk of quality regression).
Confidence metric will be a composite score combining golden-prompt pass-rate, distributional KL to FP32, and top-k token divergence; exposed as a 0-100 integer in catalog metadata.
Catalog entries will reference a calibration artifact (S3 path) and a checksum; runtime will fetch artifact and confidence before applying non-safe profile.

Automatic rollback policy: if a live metric (regression detector) trips for a model-profile pair, Console triggers a canary rollback to the 'safe' profile; define thresholds in a separate ops runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog schema v2 published and validated (fields: default_profile, backup_profile, confidence_score, calibration_artifact_uri, calibration_hash, calibration_date).

Calibration CI job that produces a deterministic artifact (quant mapping + calibration stats) for a sample of 10 representative prompts per model family completes in CI and stores artifact in S3 with checksum.
Validation harness runs end-to-end regression suite comparing FP32 vs quant profile and emits pass/fail plus confidence_score; must be reproducible locally and in CI.
Telemetry contract documented and implemented: per-call 'quant_profile_applied' event, periodic 'profile_health' aggregate with drift counters, and regression alerts wired to Console dashboards.
Rollback guardrail documented (runbook) and initial canary configured in staging for one pilot model (gptx-mini-1).
implementation_plan: 1) Define catalog schema changes and draft JSON Schema file under //confluence/model-catalog/quant-schema (artifact link in references).
2) Implement calibration CI job (Docker image + calibration harness) that accepts model binary, sample prompts, and target quant profile; outputs artifact + metrics. (owner: eng-inference)
3) Extend catalog ingestion pipeline to validate calibration_hash and attach confidence_score to model entry. (owner: eng-platform)
4) Add telemetry hooks in serving runtime to emit 'quant_profile_applied' events and aggregate health metrics. (owner: eng-runtime)
5) Create Console UI mockups to surface recommended vs safe defaults and confidence score, plus a quick 'revert to safe' button. (owner: design/PM)
6) Pilot with gptx-mini-1 (FP8 candidate) and msmall-1 (INT8 fallback) in staging; run golden prompt suite and collect telemetry for 48h. (owner: SRE + eng-qc)
7) Iterate on thresholds, publish runbook, and cut release note for runtime-1.22.
telemetry_spec: Event: quant_profile_applied -> fields: model_key, profile_id, applied_by (catalog|manual), confidence_score, calibration_hash, seq_len_distribution_tag.
Metric: profile_health.{model}.{profile}.drift_count -> increment when sample divergence crosses threshold over 1h window.
Metric: profile_accuracy.{model}.{profile}.golden_pass_rate -> percentage of golden prompts passing quality threshold (window=1000 calls).
Audit: catalog_ingestion.{model}.calibration_hash_mismatch -> emitted if stored artifact checksum differs during serving boot.
calibration_workflow: Input: model checkpoint, representative prompt set (golden suite + calibration corpus), target quant profile (FP8/INT8).
Step A: offline calibration runner produces per-layer scale factors and a quant mapping artifact plus per-prompt logits and token-diff stats.
Step B: compute confidence_score = weighted( golden_pass_rate, KL_divergence_percentile, topk_token_divergence ).
Step C: sign artifact with checksum and store to S3 path: s3://redwood-quant/calibrations/{model}/{profile}/{date}/{sha256}.tar.gz
Step D: CI validation executes full validation harness against FP32 baseline and generates report.html + machine-readable metrics.json stored alongside artifact.
validation_plan: Golden prompt suite: 120 prompts across safety, instruction-following, code-gen, long-context. Threshold: >=95% pass for 'recommended' or >=98% for 'safe' depending on model criticality.
Stat tests: KL divergence < 0.12 for token distributions over evaluation corpus; mean top-1 token change rate < 1.8%.
Statistical significance: bootstrap sampling 1k iterations to estimate CI; require 95% CI that degradation < policy threshold.
A/B rollout in staging with 10% traffic to profile for 48h, monitor profile_health and golden_pass_rate before promoting to 100%.
review_feedback: PM (R. Kim): please ensure 'confidence_score' is capped and documented; avoid users relying solely on absolute score — include calibrated percentiles.
Design (L. Chen): Console needs a tooltip explaining composite metrics; add 'why this recommendation' blurb sourced from calibration report.
SRE (M. Alvarez): guard against large S3 storms; add cache TTL and local fallback to 'safe' profile if artifact fetch fails.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting calibration prompts leading to brittle profiles. Mitigation: require cross-validation across 3 disjoint corpora and penalize overfitting in confidence_score.
Risk: Silent quality regressions in tail queries. Mitigation: promote periodic sampling of high-latency/failed requests to evaluation pipeline and increase golden suite coverage for long-tail cases.
Risk: Storage/throughput of calibration artifacts will increase. Mitigation: lifecycle policy to compress and migrate >90d artifacts to archival tier and store only latest for active models.
